questions.question: Distinguish between de facto and de jure soveriegnty.
questions.solution_html:
• Legal sovereignty –authority recognized by law –constitutional source of power –formal
  • legal supremacy –de jure sovereignty –actual political power –control over state apparatus
  • ability to enforce decisions–de facto sovereignty– difference between legal authority and real
  • power–constitutional legitimacy versus practical control –example military rule or
  • revolutionary governments.

questions.question: Discuss the arguments of pluralist theory of sovereignty.
questions.solution_html:
• Rejection of absolute sovereignty –critique of monistic state power –society composed of
  • many associations –plural centres of authority –Harold Laski G.D.H. Cole –importance of
  • voluntary associations –church, unions, guilds– state as coordinating institution
  • decentralization of power–protection of individual freedom–limits on state supremacy.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: decentralization of power–protection of individual freedom–limits on state supremacy.

questions.question: Examine the key features of Marxist approach to Political Theory.
questions.solution_html:
• Historical materialism –material conditions shape politics –economic structure determines
  • superstructure–dialectical change in history– class struggle as driving force–bourgeoisie versus
  • proletariat–conflict over means of production –inevitable social transformation
  • state as instrument of class domination –politics reflecting economic interests –ideology
  • legitimizing ruling class power– critique of capitalism–exploitation- surplus value–alienation
  • of labour –inequality in capitalist production – revolutionary transformation –proletarian
  • revolution–abolition of private property –classless communist society– withering away of the
  • state–collective ownership–egalitarian social relations–emphasis on materialist analysis.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: state–collective ownership–egalitarian social relations–emphasis on materialist analysis.

  • market oriented state functions – growth of international institutions –global governance
  • networks–policy coordination beyond national borders – expansion of security functions
  • counter terrorism measures –digital surveillance technologies – welfare delivery through
  • targeted schemes –public private partnerships –developmental governanc e models
  • digital governance and e governance –data driven policymaking –citizen service platforms
  • increased role in environmental regulation –climate policy commitments –sustainable
  • development governance – balancing economic growth social welfare security and
  • environmental responsibilities.

questions.question: Explain why democracy is considered the most advanced system of political organisation.

  • institutions–elected legislatures–accountable government–rule of law and constitutionalism
  • protection of civil liberties–fundamental rights guarantees–peaceful transfer of power–regular
  • competitive elections–political pluralism–public participation in decision making–active civil
  • society–freedom of expression –mechanisms of account ability–checks and balances
  • independent judiciary –capacity for reform adaptation –inclusion diversity representation
  • democratic legitimacy .

questions.question: Explain the concept of intersectionality in social and political analysis.
questions.solution_html:

  • forms of discrimination–intersection of race, gender, class–combined structures of oppression
  • complex social hierarchies–critique of single axis analysis–limitations of traditional feminism
  • incomplete class based analysis –power relations embedded in institutions –law, policy and
  • social practices –systemic inequality structures –recognition of marginalized experiences
  • voices of minority women , groups–inclusive social justice fram ework
  • application in public policy –equity focused governance –targeted welfare interventions
  • importance for political representation –diversity in leadership –inclusive democratic
  • participation–broader understanding of inequality –interconnected systems of privilege
